summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 43.4% YoY to INR426 crores, with same-store sales growth of 28.7% and pre-Ind AS adjusted EBITDA margin of 8.1%.
summary.overview:
United Foodbrands (Barbeque Nation) reported Q1 FY27 revenue of INR426 crores, up 43.4% YoY, with consolidated SSSG of 28.7% on top of 14.4% in Q4 FY26. Growth was volume-led (dine-in transactions up 63.5%) with no price increase taken. Pre-Ind AS adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 8.1% from about 5.5% in Q4 and roughly 350 bps higher YoY, helped by a 130 bps sequential gross margin recovery in Barbeque Nation India. International gross margin fell on Middle East-linked food inflation, and net debt rose marginally to INR106 crores.</overview>

segments.name: Barbeque Nation India
segments.commentary: Same-store sales growth 33.5%, revenue growth 43.4%, dine-in transactions up 68.6%; gross margin up ~130 bps QoQ. Captive digital ecosystem drives 65% of dine-in transactions (from ~61% in Q4); MAUs ~1.4 million, up ~60% YoY.

segments.name: Barbeque Nation International
segments.commentary: Revenue growth 46.6%, SSSG 8.5%, dine-in volume growth 45.2%, gross profit up 40.3%. Restaurant operating margin 18.7%, but gross margin down ~3 pp on Middle East-linked inflation; added 1 UAE restaurant.

segments.name: Premium casual dining (Premium CDR)
segments.commentary: Revenue growth ~36%, SSSG 13.6%, dine-in volume growth ~40%. Mature restaurants deliver restaurant operating margin of upwards of 20%; added 1 and closed 1 restaurant, network unchanged. Q4 FY26 cohort expected to lift segment margin.

guidance_outlook: SSSG expected to moderate through FY27 as comparables tighten, with Q3 and Q4 FY27 lapping the strongest quarter of FY26; management called this a base effect, not weaker demand.

Margin levers for FY27: gross margin recovery in India, mature portfolio ROM expansion, new-store cohort maturation and back-end cost leverage; management did not give a pre-Ind AS double-digit EBITDA margin timeline.
Target of 300 restaurants by FY27 (about 40 additions this year vs ~35 last year); 15 restaurants under construction to operationalise in Q2 and Q3 FY27.
FY27 capex guided at ~INR140 crores (INR120 crores for new outlets, INR20 crores maintenance and ancillary), per the prior guidance reiterated on the call.
Management sees Barbeque Nation India capable of ~600 restaurants at current scale, up from an earlier view of 400-450, given the Big Buffet format in Tier 2/3 markets.
Momentum said to be continuing into July; revenue crossed INR400 crores for the first time, and the quarter ended at about INR425 crores.
capex_capacity: Restaurant count closed Q1 FY27 at 266 after 5 additions; target of 300 by FY27 maintained.
15 restaurants under construction, expected to open in Q2 and Q3 FY27.
Barbeque Nation India store format reduced to ~3,500 sq ft from 4,500 sq ft; newer format's revenue per restaurant said to be among the highest.
Expansion funded largely from internal accruals; borrowings to be kept at prudent levels.
demand_pricing: Growth described as entirely volume-led; no price increase taken in Q1 despite inflation. Average per-cover spend declined due to value initiatives from Q2 FY26 and has now stabilised at Q4 FY26 levels.
Average revenue per mature restaurant is around INR7 crores; management has not given a target for the next step.
Repeat business is ~45-47% of the base, with the new-vs-repeat mix shifting slightly toward new guests. Average bill is ~4.3 pax, and repeat tracking relies on one mobile number per bill.

Delivery growth of 62% was supported by value SKUs across Barbeque Nation, BBQ and Dum Safar brands and by higher marketing spend. Delivery share of mix rose ~2 pp YoY and carries commission and packaging costs of about 30%.
Management described the mature cost base as 'normalised' after recent hires in culinary, marketing and digital; each INR1 per-cover improvement adds about INR1.5 crores of annual cost impact.
